wpm-interpreter.title: Check what your WPM means
wpm-interpreter.intro: Enter a result from any typing test. The interpretation uses practical learning bands, not population percentiles. A speed is only useful at the accuracy and duration you can sustain.
wpm-interpreter.staticText: The interactive version accepts WPM, accuracy and test duration. It does not estimate a population percentile or reproduce an exam's scoring.

bands.label: Starting out
bands.note: You are still locating keys. Work on the home row and clean keystrokes before chasing speed.

bands.label: Developing
bands.note: You can type normal text, but you may still look at the keyboard often. Finger placement and accuracy are the next wins.

bands.label: Functional
bands.note: Enough for many study and entry-level tasks. Build toward 40 WPM without sacrificing accuracy.

bands.label: Comfortable
bands.note: A practical range for regular email, notes and office work.

bands.label: Fast
bands.note: A strong everyday speed if accuracy stays high. Use a longer test to confirm you can sustain it.

bands.label: Very fast
bands.note: Well above typical office demands. Gains now come from consistency, symbols and accuracy.

targets.label: Comfortable office work
targets.detail: A common practical target, not an official rule.

targets.label: MP CPCT typing, English
targets.detail: 30 NWPM is the minimum passing band in the published rulebook.

targets.label: RRB NTPC typist posts, English
targets.detail: Historical CBTST standard under CEN 06/2025; the 2026 CENs dispensed the test for the notified posts.

durationNotes.1: One minute is a short burst. Use it to warm up or measure pace, not to predict a 10-minute exam result.
durationNotes.2: Two minutes is still a short sample. Use it as a pace check rather than a sustained benchmark.
durationNotes.3: Three minutes starts to show sustained speed, but fatigue over a longer test can still lower the number.
durationNotes.5: Five minutes is a useful sustained benchmark for everyday and office typing.
durationNotes.10: Ten minutes matches the length of several Indian typing skill tests, including SSC CHSL LDC/JSA.
durationNotes.15: Fifteen minutes matches the MP CPCT typing modules and is a strong endurance check.

accuracyNotes.high: Strong accuracy. A speed at this level is usable in real work and gives you room inside typical exam error limits.
accuracyNotes.medium: Workable accuracy, but keep watching the error count. Exam rules can still fail a fast run with too many mistakes.
accuracyNotes.low: Treat the speed as provisional. Errors and corrections eat into usable output, and many exams count mistakes separately.

wpm-interpreter.note: These reference points are for orientation. Exam scoring, language, duration and error rules differ; use your own notification.

finger-map.title: Keyboard finger map
finger-map.intro: Each key belongs to one finger. The home keys are A, S, D and F for the left hand, and J, K, L and ; for the right hand. Return each finger to its home key after every reach.

home-row-drill.title: One-minute home-row drill
home-row-drill.text: This drill uses home-row words only. It starts when you click, so it will not capture keystrokes while you read. Keep your eyes on the screen and return each finger to its home key after every reach.
home-row-drill.staticText: The interactive drill starts only after you press the start button. Until then, it does not listen for keystrokes.
